structure: Part 6, Animal identification, read in full at repos/trade-imports-animals-frontend main 4c2119da. Paths are under src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/: page.js (the page's id animalIdentification and slug commodities/identification), evaluation.js (how the page's per-animal fields bind to obligations), copy/copy.en.js and copy/copy.cy.js (only the identification block is this part's; the search and consignmentDetails blocks belong to part 5), the whole animal-identification folder (animal-identification.controller.js; the page template animal-identification.njk; the partials _identification-card.njk, _selected-commodities-summary.njk and _saved-animals-table.njk; fields.js; form/forms.js; remove/post-remove.js; records/append.js; card/error-summary.js; card/view-model.js; identifier/fields.js; identifier/table.js; address/fields.js; summary/selected-commodities.js), fit/identification.fit.spec.js (30 tests in 6 describe blocks, three of them parameterised over 5, 6 and 8 cases) and fit/axe.js. consignment-details/validation/count-drop.js was opened only to confirm that the count-drop error link lands on this page's card. The page (/commodities/identification, heading Identification details) shows a section caption, an inset, a Selected commodities summary table of every commodity line with a Change link per row, an Add another commodity link, then one card per commodity line whose commodity declares at least one identifier. Each card has a title, a Change number of animals link, a saved-animals table once a record exists, then either a counter-headed entry form for the next animal (the commodity's identifier fields in the commodity's own order and, where the commodity takes one, a permanent-address block with a fraud warning, a definition and eight fields) or an all-entered or over-count message, and an in-card save button whose wording depends on how many animals are left. The page ends on the shared Save and continue actions. A consignment with no identifiable line never sees the page. Claims cover the route, reach and redirects, every field with label, hint and when it is required, every validation message verbatim, add, remove and cap behaviour, what is saved and how it binds to obligations, the error summary, the Welsh copy and its status, and every test in the spec. Claim ids 001 to 129 keep the ids of this slice's earlier extract (same prefix, same HEAD), each re-checked against the files; 130 onwards are new. Unit tests (*.test.js) were not in the read list and are not claimed.
